verdict.rationale: Entra's application management docs say admins can configure an application's permissions, tokens, and certificates. That is the product's own mechanism for credentialed, permission-bounded app access, but the evidence describes it only in a single high-level line. The Actor-token community comment concerns Microsoft-internal tokens, not customer-issued credentials, so it does not create a dispute. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of issuing client secrets or certificates for a non-human or agent identity, granular least-privilege scope or role assignment, credential expiry and rotation, and any agent-specific identity feature or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent
